text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New child tax benefit planned: Ottawa, provinces to meet on deal that would help working poor, free funds for day care.
- Crombie calls swap of services unwise: Urges province to reconsider.
- Wage gap narrows between women, men: Canadians earned less over all in 1995 as men lost high-paying jobs.
- Separatists can be replaced, Black says: Media magnate warns Canada to make no more concessions to Quebec.
- Nunavut appointment a political hot potato: Critics worry that commissioner's job could become patronage plum for Liberal backbencher.
- Onex joins auto parts elite: Subsidiary's C$625-million acquisition of A.O. Smith unit creates a metal stamping leader.
- Plans to boost power exports challenged: Utilities' rival ask U.S. to reject bids.
- Auto firms bend to new process: Using water pressure, plants produce metal parts that weigh less, have fewer pieces and are more uniform - at a lower cost.
- Canadian Pacific posts record profit: 1996 earnings C$829.1 million.
- Avenor eyes C$850-million sale: If its C$3.3-billion takeover bid Repap goes through, Avenor will sell all assets of both companies in B.C. and Manitoba and look for synergies elsewhere.
- Onex's Tower Corp. drives into big leagues with US$625-million deal.
